name: URL Shortener Resolver
description: Resolve known HTTP(S) URL shorteners into a standard shortened-link object.
requirements: Direct outbound HTTP(S) on ports 80/443 and system DNS resolution
features: Match the starting hostname against a built-in exact-match shortener list. Use additional_shorteners for custom or branded domains. Subsequent destinations need not be shorteners.

Follow HTTP 301, 302, 303, 307 and 308 redirects, including relative and scheme-relative Location headers. Preserve query strings, percent-encode Unicode paths and queries, normalize hostnames using non-transitional IDNA2008/UTS #46 with strict label validation, and inherit fragments when Location omits one.
Use HEAD; retry with GET only when HEAD returns 405 or 501. Read response headers only and close each response without downloading its body.

Validate every hop and every fallback request against all DNS answers. Reject non-public, multicast, reserved, IPv4-mapped and mixed public/private answers. Connect to a validated address with the original Host header, TLS hostname verification and CA verification.
Reject credentials, non-HTTP(S) schemes, nonstandard ports, malformed URLs, redirect loops, missing Location headers and HTTP failures. No partial expansion is returned on failure.
Preserve the original attribute UUID, comment, tags and to_ids setting. All generated object attributes have to_ids=false.

output.redirect-url: The final URL that returned a successful 2xx response after at least one redirect.
output.text: JSON containing an ordered redirects array, with url, redirect-url, status and method for every hop. Intermediate URLs remain in this history rather than becoming independent indicators.
output.reference: The shortened-link object is derived-from the original URL attribute UUID.
output.errors: Invalid input/configuration, unknown shorteners, no redirect, DNS/network/TLS failures, unsafe destinations, HTTP failures, loops and exhausted limits return an error.

additional_shorteners.description: Comma-separated exact hostnames, for example go.example.org,s.example.net. Hostnames only; no schemes, ports, paths, wildcards or empty entries. Matching is case-insensitive and normalizes IDNA and trailing dots.

max_redirects.description: Maximum redirects to follow. Positive integer; accepts MISP configuration strings. Exactly this number of redirects may be followed, plus the final response.

timeout.description: Positive integer seconds per HTTP request, including connect/read time. This is not a wall-clock budget for the whole expansion or a bound on system DNS resolution. HEAD fallback may add one request per hop.

installation: The module is automatically discovered at misp_modules/modules/expansion/url_shortener.py. Its dependencies are already core dependencies of misp-modules; no API key or new Python package is needed.
Restart misp-modules and enable url_shortener in MISP's Enrichment plugin settings. Expand a URL attribute using its existing UUID.
Use the existing shortened-link object template (UUID 361c0ae8-68bd-11e8-adc0-fa7ae01bbebc). Update MISP's object templates if it is absent. No new template or change to misp-objects is necessary.
Outbound connections use validated IPs directly. Deploy with suitable DNS and direct HTTP(S) egress; this module does not use environment proxies or proxy credentials.
limitations: This performs live requests to the shortener and destination: both can observe the module server's IP address and URL token. It is not passive enrichment.

JavaScript redirects, HTML meta refresh, authentication flows, cookies, interstitial pages and CAPTCHAs are not processed. A HEAD 2xx response is terminal even if a browser GET would behave differently.
Shortener services can retire or change behavior; membership in the built-in list does not guarantee availability. Subdomains and www variants require their own exact entry.
Only the first validated public DNS address is attempted. No retries, alternate-address failover or persistent cookies are used.
An unknown shortener or a known shortener returning no redirect produces an explanatory error. A destination returning a non-2xx response is not reported as a successfully resolved URL.

verification.scope: Mocked DNS/HTTP responses, strict shortened-link template validation, module discovery, URL handling, source preservation, cleanup, fallback, limits, network errors and public-address enforcement. Live shortener services and a running MISP deployment have not been tested.
